items.stimulus: Many older European cities grew outward from a central marketplace, so their streets radiate like spokes and nearly every route leads toward the center. Many North American cities, ______, were laid out on a rectangular grid before settlers arrived, so their streets run in parallel lines and no single point draws traffic toward it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Both sentences use the same frame: a group of cities, then how its streets are laid out. The subjects differ (European cities and North American cities), and the attribute flips: in one, streets radiate toward a center, and in the other, they form a grid with no center. Two things set side by side with opposite features call for a contrast word, so 'by contrast' is correct.

D.why: You read the second sentence as a result of the first. How European cities grew doesn't cause North American cities to use grids. The two are compared, and neither causes the other.
